summary: MPI-443 made npm test + npm run test:desktop a release gate, but the gate is a human step in mpi-version-bump - nothing runs the suites on push. A windows-latest runner can run BOTH today: Electron needs no xvfb on Windows, and Playwright drives it through the electron npm binary, so no npx playwright install step is needed. The one blocker is real and must be decided first: package.json line 28 pins "@cubric/connector": "file:../Cubric-Studio/packages/connector", a sibling path that does not exist on a lone checkout, so npm ci fails before any test runs. Three ways out, all needing a call from the user: (a) a second actions/checkout of the private MadPonyInteractive/Cubric-Studio repo with a PAT secret, (b) publish @cubric/connector to a registry, (c) vendor it into this repo. Note the existing .github/workflows/build-portable.yml runs NO tests - it only dispatches the private mpi-ci build on a v* tag, so a red suite currently cannot stop a build.

Investigated the three options and found a fourth that beats all of them. dist/ is untracked in Cubric-Studio so a private checkout would also need a tsc build; vendoring would fork an interop contract against the documented ownership split. But all three consumers already dynamic-import the SDK inside try/catch and handle its absence by design (brokerBoot.js returns null with an SDK-not-installed comment), so it is an OPTIONAL dependency declared as a hard one. Moving it out of dependencies unblocks npm ci with no secret, no registry and no copy, and may also fix the shipped macOS dangling-symlink bug on MPI-416. Needs testing on a repo copy before committing - a missing file: target may still break lockfile resolution even under optionalDependencies.

Schema fix only, no scope change: maturity was "todo", which is not in the enum - <mpi-lib>/task-board-ops/_schema.md allows idea, planned, research, needs-decision, blocked or deferred for the todo column, and the board UI was flagging it as invalid. Set to planned: the card is understood work with a testable next step (option d on a repo copy), not blocked on an external wait and no longer waiting on a user call.

Picked up. Consumers re-verified: server.js:146, services/brokerBoot.js:61 and services/connectorResponder.js:80 all dynamic-import @cubric/connector inside try/catch and return null on failure, so option (d) is sound in principle. Next step is the npm ci test on a repo COPY outside c:/AI/Mpi so the sibling is genuinely absent.

The stated blocker is FALSE and no package.json change is needed. npm ci exits 0 on a lone checkout with the UNMODIFIED package.json - npm 11.9.0 does not fail on a missing file: target, it creates a dangling symlink. Verified on a package.json+lock copy outside c:/AI/Mpi and on a real git clone (tracked files only, what actions/checkout gets): npm ci exit 0 and the full 417-test suite green. optionalDependencies was measured too and changes nothing (still a dangling symlink, still exit 0), so option (d) also would NOT have fixed the macOS artifact bug - that finding is recorded on MPI-416, where copyAppTree was confirmed to copy the symlink verbatim. THE REAL BLOCKER WAS A FLAKY TEST: the first clone run failed extra-model-folders.test.cjs and passed on re-run. Root cause is a race, not a clean checkout - node --test runs test FILES in parallel and both extra-model-folders.test.cjs and settings-models-root-guard.test.cjs POST /comfy/set-path, which rewrites the single global extra_model_paths.yaml that getCustomRoot() reads base_path back out of. Fixed structurally: each file now sets CUBRIC_ENGINE_ROOT to its own mkdtemp dir before routes/comfy captures ENGINE_ROOT, so the shared state is gone (no retry, no concurrency cap). The suite also stops rewriting the developer's real engine yaml - mtime verified unchanged. Added .github/workflows/tests.yml on windows-latest (npm ci, npm test, npm run test:desktop, test-results/ uploaded on failure), triggering on push to master AND to bare release branches [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]* - a hotfix there never touches master but still gets a v* tag build. Tag coupling DECIDED: build-portable.yml stays decoupled, since a tag is cut from a commit tests.yml already ran and mpi-version-bump keeps its human gate. Remaining: prove a red suite fails the workflow, which needs a push and the user's go-ahead.
